content.title: Rory McIlroy net worth soared to enormous new heights after winning Masters
content.text: Rory McIlroy has seen his net worth increase by almost $50 million in the last 12 months, according to the Sunday Times Rich List, ranking among the wealthiest under-40s in the UK15:43 ET, 12 Apr 2026Updated 15:43 ET, 12 Apr 2026Rory McIlroy's wealth has grown substantially over the past year, according to a wide-ranging rich list.The latest Sunday Times Rich List in the UK released last year placed his net worth at approximately $350 million, representing a jump of nearly $50 million compared to the previous year. The highly regarded list, now celebrating its 37th year, spotlights the 350 wealthiest individuals across the United Kingdom.McIlroy ranks among the richest under-40s in the UK, claiming the 19th spot on that particular list, placing him ahead of Harry Styles. He is now looking to claim another Green Jacket, after getting brutally honest with Amanda Balionis after a Masters round he didn't want.Football historian Steve Bolton analyses first footage of women's gameREAD MORE: Masters security crackdown launched as influencers threaten strict ruleREAD MORE: Rory McIlroy drives on range catch attention after dismal Masters roundThe 36-year-old's actual fortune is likely even higher, as the list does not take bank balances into account. Instead, it is based on identifiable assets, including land, property, art, racehorses, and significant stakes in publicly traded companies.Last month, McIlroy achieved the career Grand Slam by clinching the Masters title following a sudden-death playoff. His victory at Augusta earned him $4.2 million, pushing his total PGA Tour earnings to just under $105 million.The list was put together by business journalist Robert Watts, who noted: "The Sunday Times Rich List is changing. Our billionaire count is down and the combined wealth of those who feature in our research is falling. We are also finding fewer of the world's super rich are coming to live in the UK.You agree you are 18 or over. More info"Our research continues to find a wide variety of self-made entrepreneurs building fortunes not just from artificial intelligence, video games and new technologies, but also mundane, everyday items such as makeup, radiators and jogging bottoms."We know many of our readers find these people and their stories inspiring - especially the many who had tough starts or setbacks to their lives and careers."McIlroy entered the final day at Augusta National as joint-leader alongside Cameron Young. After a tough third day, that saw his big lead evaporated, McIlroy said: "There's a long way to go."Yeah, this golf course has a way of, you know, when you're not quite feeling it, you struggle. You have to dig deep, and I felt like I did that on the front nine and made a lot of good par saves."Missed a couple of chances on eight and nine; then I thought I turned the round around with the birdie on ten. Then I felt like I hit a pretty good second shot on 11. It just drifted on the wind a little bit and went in the water. Those two holes weren't great."But again, I felt like I bounced back pretty well with the birdies on 14 and 15. It would have been nice to play those last few holes and not make that bogey on 17, but you know, I still have a great chance. I'm in the final group. I just need to go to the range and try to figure it out a little bit."
